extracted.intended_audience: general entertainment/TV-news readers interested in documentaries and comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A short entertainment news piece summarizing and evaluating the newly released trailer for a comedy-focused docuseries, highlighting subject matter, participants, tone, and likely audience reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth beyond punchlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The series should 'go beyond the punchlines' and not stay at surface-level jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece emphasizes that the documentary will investigate darker, less comedic aspects of comedians' lives rather than just their performances; examples include exploring drugs, guns, shame and internal struggles. Aim for substantive behind-the-scenes material rather than only clips of stand-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative/‘deep dive’ scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The production should perform a 'deep dive into the good, the bad, and the ugly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative focus means tracing complexities and contradictions in subjects' lives, presenting a rounded portrait that includes both achievements and troubling elements. The article treats this investigative angle as a defining and positive characteristic of the franchise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candor and willingness to 'hold nothing back'
rubrics_metrics.description: The show should be candid, unflinching, and willing to disclose 'hard-to-learn details.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trailer and article praise an unsparing approach — frank testimony from participants, disclosures about personal demons, and confronting uncomfortable truths. Canonical topics cited: substance abuse, weapons, shame, private struggles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonal balance: equal parts funny and dark
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a balance between humor and darkness — described as 'equal parts funny and, well… dark.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece flags the importance of preserving comedic material and recognizable humor while interrogating darker backstage realities; tone should neither be purely comedic nor solely sensationalistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of credible participants and narrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature familiar, credible voices from the comedy world (subjects, peers, and a recognizable narrator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article lists many named comedians (e.g., Andrew Dice Clay, Chris Farley, Maria Bamford, Patton Oswalt) and notes Dave Foley as narrator; inclusion of respected insiders lends authority and context to the documentary's claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of perspectives / notable subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover multiple well-known figures across comedy to provide breadth and comparative perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trailer includes a 'slew of familiar faces' and both subjects and participants; breadth across different careers and eras gives the series more scope and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection: focus on the 'underbelly' / trauma of public figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose topics that reveal the underbelly of the art form — trauma, personal struggles, and industry pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this focus as a strategic editorial choice consistent with other franchise entries (Dark Side of the Ring, Dark Side of Football) and suggests that audiences are drawn to that investigative framing of public figures' traumas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise precedent and format success
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage the franchise’s prior track record (e.g., Dark Side of the Ring) as an indicator of potential success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses past seasons' performance (three seasons, strong fan interest) as an implicit standard — a new installment should follow the format that proved successful (deep investigative episodes focused on famous, troubled subjects) to achieve similar results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement as success metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Success is measured by audience interest in learning 'what goes on behind the curtain.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece treats fan appetite for behind-the-scenes revelations and ratings/engagement for the franchise as the practical metric by which the new series will be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional timing and release positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate trailer release and premiere scheduling to maximize visibility (e.g., trailer drop and August 16 premiere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article mentions the trailer drop and premiere date/time as part of coverage; timely promotion and clear release information are treated as part of the series rollout strategy that affects reception.
